identification.description: Thorny shrub or small tree with opposite leaves, white fragrant flowers and globose fruits.
identification.whole_plant: Small tree or shrub, often armed with paired thorns.
identification.stem: Woody and branched, commonly bearing paired spines.
identification.leaf: Simple, opposite, elliptic to obovate leaves.
identification.flower: White, fragrant, tubular flowers, usually in axillary clusters.
identification.fruit: Globose berry-like fruit, green when young and yellowish when mature.
identification.seed: Numerous hard seeds embedded in pulp.

therapeutics.precautions: Madanaphala has a specific emetic-drug role; dosing and procedure must be taken from an authenticated classical/official protocol, not this educational record.

modern_information.evidence_summary: Randia dumetorum is primarily notable in Ayurveda as a classical emetic drug; modern use should not be inferred from that traditional role.
modern_information.safety_notes: Emetic action can be clinically significant. Do not self-administer or infer a dose from this site.
